text:
incident-bot: :pager: Paging on-call: p99 streaming latency breach detected for single-tenant ArborHealth (tenant_id=ah-42). Alert: p99 18.6s, p95 2.4s. Root cause unknown.

ashley: I'm on it. grabbing logs and metrics now. anyone already looking into KV cache stats?

devon: seeing a big spike in concurrent sessions from ArborHealth in the last 5m — ~4x usual. Could be fanout + long prompt prefixes.

samir: confirmed. traces show a lot of requests hitting long-prefix paths (avg prefix tokens ~280). Streaming stalls show many "waiting for kvload" in runtime logs.

kate: tagging @arbor-support to let them know we're investigating customer impact. @ashley you want me to draft a message?

arbor-support: thx. Customer opened a support ticket reporting slow real-time summaries for patients. They're in production, high priority. Any ETA?

ashley: short update to ArborSupport: "we're investigating a tail latency regression affecting streaming for a subset of your requests (large prefixes + high concurrency). Will follow up with mitigation steps in ~15m."

devon: quick prometheus query snippets i'm running:
```
# 5m p99 for arborth-streaming
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="ah-42"}[5m])) by (le))
# KV cache miss rate
sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total{tenant="ah-42"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total{tenant="ah-42"}[5m]))
```

samir: results: p99 18.6s, kv cache miss rate 0.72 (very high). heatmap shows a burst of long prefixes correlating with misses. Looks like cache thrash and oversized prefixes causing blocking on disk-backed KV loads.

ashley: live mitigation options: 1) temporarily rate-limit concurrent requests from ArborHealth, 2) route ArborHealth to warm-pool instances with more memory, 3) enable short-circuit policy to fallback to smaller model variant for requests with >200 prefix tokens, 4) pre-warm KV for top-k prefixes. Which is fastest?

devon: fastest = 1 + 3. We can flip a routing rule to attach a concurrency limiter in the edge for tenant ah-42 in ~2m. Fallback to smaller model is config toggle (model-variant-rollout) and should be safe for short term.

kate: i can do the customer comms. recommend we ask arbor for non-urgent workloads to pause while we mitigate.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of model-variant small-embed started by devops-quickfix. ID: dv-2026-38.

ashley: ok doing step 1: applying edge limiter to 10rps per shard for ah-42. command:
```
redwoodctl route update --tenant ah-42 --concurrency-limit 10
```

(ashley adds) applied — edge is enforcing 10rps, traffic dropped ~60% and p95 improved to 1.9s within 90s. p99 still elevated at 6.2s.

devon: good. now enabling fallback for long prefixes (>200 tokens) to small variant. command:
```
redwoodctl rollout set --tenant ah-42 --route "*" --condition "prefix_len>200" --model small-variant-v3 --weight 100
```

samir: toggled fallback. watching traces. initial samples show fewer streaming stalls, kv cache miss rate dropping to 0.28. p99 sliding towards 2.8s.

arbor-support: customer confirms degraded but usable; they accept temporary fallback if it reduces latency. Thank you.

kate: drafting to customer: "We applied short-term mitigations: concurrency limits and a model fallback for very long prefixes to stabilize tail latency. We're continuing to reduce p99 and will follow up with root cause and permanent fix." want to include any runbook steps?

ashley: add that we're investigating KV cache sizing and will consider pre-warm and cache admission changes.

devon: digging deeper — some of the long prefixes are highly unique (PHI redaction prompts) which prevent cache reuse. For those, fallback is acceptable until we provide a dedicated warm pool with increased KV memory.

samir: proposal for next steps: short-term (today) - keep concurrency limiter and conditional fallback enabled until traffic normalizes; medium-term (48-72h) - allocate warm-pool nodes for ah-42 with larger KV budget + add prefix pre-warm for top 500 prefixes; long-term - evaluate admission policies and prefix normalization to improve cache hit rate.

ashley: agree. i'll keep on-call until handoff at +4h. @devon @samir can you file a post-incident task with the KV sizing numbers and traces? include prometheus + trace ids.

devon: filing task now -> INC-2213456789-kv-sizing (assign samir + devon). attaching graphs and trace IDs.

ops-bot: incident log updated. mitigation: edge limiter applied, model fallback enabled, warm-pool request submitted.

kate: on customer comms channel: sent initial note and asked them to flag if they see errors or quality regressions.

arbor-support: customer replied: "we see much better latency, minor change in generation quality on long summaries is acceptable for now."

ashley: marking incident as mitigated for now. monitoring for 30m. will update status and schedule RCA.

samir: quick snippet of logs we saw earlier (for RCA):
```
2026-03-15T14:22:03Z runtime[worker-7]: req=0x7f3c prefix_len=312 kv_load=cache_miss disk_io=1 blocked=TRUE wait_ms=18234
2026-03-15T14:22:04Z runtime[worker-9]: req=0x8a1b prefix_len=298 kv_load=cache_miss disk_io=1 blocked=TRUE wait_ms=17491
```

devon: noted. we'll look at admission thresholds and maybe normalize tokens (truncate or summarize prefixes) before serving to reduce unique prefix cardinality.

ashley: thanks team. i'll hand off to @devon for overnight watch in ~3.5h. good job. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident severity updated -> mitigated. paging suppressed. Please follow up with RCA in the incident tracker.
